target.name: runtime-installed IWRAM ten-bit field clamp and de-interleave
target.role: a field conversion and de-interleave: two ten-bit signed fields per source word, each saturated to signed 8-bit, packed into two destination halfword streams while the source pair is zeroed in place
target.notes: THE OVERLAY'S ONLY SATURATING CONVERSION, AND THE ANSWER TO THE BRIEF'S 'EIGHT SHIFT SITES SUMMING TO 38'. The routine reads two source words, ZEROES THEM IN PLACE, and writes one halfword to each of two destination cursors: each source word carries TWO ten-bit SIGNED fields, at bits 31..22 and at bits 15..6, and bits 21..16 and 5..0 are never read by any instruction. Each field is saturated to signed 8-bit [-128,127] and packed as one byte, with the two LOW fields going to the first destination and the two HIGH fields to the second - a DE-INTERLEAVE of a two-channel interleaved stream, not a conversion of one stream. THE SHIFT SITES: there are EIGHT and their amounts are 22, 22, 16, 16, 22, 22, 8, 8, summing to 136 and not 38. The 38 is a TWO-SITE PAIR SUM rather than a total, and the previous census's own field names it: `same_register_opposite_shift` printed `amount(nearest opposite-direction shift on the same source register) + amount(this site)`, which for the low-field extractor is `lsl #16` + `asr #22 = 38`, printed at six of the eight sites. Eight non-zero amounts of at least 8 cannot total 38. The pair is also not a net `>> 6`: the intermediate 32-bit logical shift DISCARDS bits 31..16 so that the arithmetic shift sign-extends from bit 15, which is what makes it a ten-bit field rather than a six-bit one. Reading those two instructions as one net shift is the error the brief's number came from. THE SATURATION IS FOUR INSTRUCTIONS and the pattern `cmp #0x7F ; movgt #0x7F ; cmn #0x80 ; mvnlt #0x7F` occurs exactly once in the whole 8 MiB image, so this unit is the only clamp in the overlay; ARMv4T has no ssat/usat, so a saturation can only be a conditional move. THE TWO LOW values are explicitly masked with `and #0xFF` before the `orr`; the two HIGH values are not, because the `strh` keeps only the low 16 bits - the missing mask is a property of the store width. THE COUNT is a do-while over word PAIRS with a SIGNED greater-than test, so the body always runs at least once whatever the count is, and an odd count over-reads one word: a count of 3 consumes four words and runs twice. There is no bound on the source pointer. Reproduced, not repaired. THE FINGERPRINT that finds it is the POST-INDEXED store to two cursor registers; 'two halfword destination bases' alone is not enough, because the IRQ dispatcher also has two and neither of its stores advances. See docs/LIFT_IWRAM_NUMERIC.md.
